item.title: Quantum Phases and Structural Transitions of Bosons in Bubble-Shaped Confinements
item.description: arXiv:2610.30381v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the structural properties and superfluid behavior of soft-core bosons confined in a spherical bubble trap at large particle numbers ($N \le 1800$). Using Path Integral Monte Carlo simulations with worm algorithm sampling in continuous space, we show that increasing $N$ drives a sequence of layering transitions: beyond the established bilayer supersolid, a third concentric layer of clusters emerges at $N \approx 1800$. By analyzing the distribution of permutation cycles distribution, we demonstrate that a finite superfluid fraction ($f_s \approx 10\%$) persists even in this multi-layer regime. These findings clarify the role of particle number in driving layer formation on curved manifolds, offering a concrete guide for future experiments with bubble-trapped bosons.
item.dc:creator: Fabio Cinti, Gabriele Costa, Giuseppe Pellicane, Santi Prestipino, Matteo Ciardi

item.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.31185v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.
item.dc:creator: Wan-Ling Yang, Shao-Bo Liu, Xiang Luo, Chao Yang, Hai-Lin Li, Yu-Zhou Yang, Yong-Kui Wang, Bing Yang

item.title: Breathing and quadrupole modes in squeezed Bose-Bose liquid drops
item.description: arXiv:2610.31581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the lowest excitation modes of binary $^{39}$K ultradilute droplets confined harmonically in one direction, which reduces the critical number of particles needed to sustain a self-bound state. Using the density functional built from first-principles quantum Monte Carlo calculations (QMC), which incorporates the effects of finite range interactions, we study the crossover of the oscillation modes from three to two dimensions. For weak squeezing, we observe the coupling between breathing and quadrupole modes, resulting from the breaking of spherical symmetry. Increasing the squeezing, the higher-frequency mode corresponding to three-dimensional breathing mode becomes unstable. For squeezings stronger and comparable to experiments, we analyze the dependence of the excitation modes on the droplet size for several interactions and show the reduction of the number of particles needed to sustain stable oscillations. The differences between the results obtained with the QMC functional and the extended Gross-Pitaevskii theory are increased with respect to the case of previously studied spherical droplets.
item.dc:creator: Marko Korda, Leandra Vranje\v{s} Marki\'c, Jordi Boronat

item.title: Discrete time liquids
item.description: arXiv:2610.30266v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete time crystals exhibit robust subharmonic oscillations, spontaneously breaking the discrete time-translation symmetry of a periodic drive. Since their emergence, the question of whether other types of temporal many-body order can exist has attracted considerable attention. Here we identify discrete time liquids -- a new form of spatiotemporal order characterized by short-range temporal coherence as a result of time-solitons. We study a two-dimensional spin system coupled to a finite-temperature cavity, whose fluctuations provide a noisy, approximately periodic drive with only finite temporal coherence. Remarkably, the spins nevertheless form a metastable state with robust period-doubled dynamics over an extended parameter regime. Unlike a time crystal, this state has only finite temporal coherence: individual trajectories stochastically switch between the two symmetry-related temporal configurations of the period-doubled response. We identify these switches as time-solitons: topological defects in temporal order that preserve local period doubling while destroying long-range temporal coherence, thereby producing the time liquid state. We propose a minimal model which reproduces the distribution of temporal correlations of the many-body system, suggesting a general description of the time liquid as a time crystal with a finite density of time-solitons. Because these solitons can occur at arbitrary times, ensemble averaging restores continuous time-translation symmetry, raising the intriguing possibility that discrete time liquids can exist in thermal equilibrium.
item.dc:creator: Zuo Wang, Paul M. Schindler, Marin Bukov, Marios H. Michael

item.title: Time-reversal-based quantum metrology in a central-spin architecture: from SATIN to butterfly echo
item.description: arXiv:2610.30686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate quantum-enhanced time-reversal-based metrology using the central spin model, in which a single ancilla spin of magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ mediates interactions between $N$ bath spins through a star-graph topology. We demonstrate that the SATIN (Signal Amplification Through Time-reversal Interaction) echo protocol can be implemented in this setup to achieve a Fisher information of $N^2/e$ with the collective $\langle J_y\rangle$ readout, corresponding to a $4.34\,\mathrm{dB}$ offset from the Heisenberg limit. Furthermore, we establish that this platform provides a pathway to perform the butterfly echo protocol by conjugating each evolution step with a random collective bath rotation, thereby achieving axis-agnostic Heisenberg-scaled sensing. Crucially, with a small $N-$independent number of random steps, the butterfly echo reaches a Fisher information of $N^2/4$ ($6\,\mathrm{dB}$ below the Heisenberg limit) for any unknown encoding axis, with the plateau gain tracking the Haar limit. Finally, we demonstrate that the central-spin magnitude $S_{\rm cen}$ provides a powerful knob to reduce the optimal protocol timescale without altering the metrological ceiling or the circuit depth required to reach isotropy. The proposed scheme is relevant to cavity QED and NMR quantum processors, where the central spin architecture arises naturally.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kumar, Sayan Choudhury

item.title: The often overlooked role of sound in liquid thermal transport
item.description: arXiv:2610.31127v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Formulated a hundred years ago, the Bridgman formula for thermal conductivity of liquids postulates a proportionality between sound velocity and thermal conductivity. This designates phonons as heat carriers in a liquid. Its empirical success has been under-appreciated and its conceptual implications overlooked. It is not mentioned in well-known condensed-matter textbook. Here, we review its origin, its links to hydrodynamic Euler equations and to the fundamental paradox surrounding the parabolic heat equation and its fate across the quantum-classical crossover.
item.dc:creator: Kamran Behnia

item.title: Sign-problem-free Bosonic Auxiliary Field Quantum Monte Carlo
item.description: arXiv:2610.31541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The sign problem poses a fundamental barrier to numerically exact quantum Monte Carlo simulations, severely hindering our understanding of quantum many-body physics across disciplines ranging from condensed matter to particle and nuclear physics. Geometrical frustration makes this barrier especially acute for interacting bosons. Here, we develop a bosonic auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (BAFQMC) method and rigorously prove that time-reversal symmetry and reflection positivity each provide a general sufficient condition for sign-problem-free simulations. Crucially, under either criterion, BAFQMC evades the sign problem even on frustrated lattices where conventional world-line and stochastic-series-expansion methods fail. Benchmarking our approach on a two-flavor Bose-Hubbard model on the triangular lattice yields excellent quantitative agreement with finite-temperature exact diagonalization. By establishing unifying principles to solve the sign problem in BAFQMC, our work substantially expands the reach of unbiased, numerically exact simulations for frustrated bosonic matter.
item.dc:creator: Yin-Kai Yu, Zhong-Chao Wei, Zi-Xiang Li

item.title: Occupancy Driven Phase Transitions in Gapped Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.31564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Systems characterized by an energy gap between the ground state and excited states support a growing number of thermal excitations upon raising the temperature. Provided these excitations interact with each other, their number affects the size of the energy gap akin to a harmonic oscillator where the oscillation frequency is damping dependent. Here we show that once a critical number of excitations is reached, the excitation population becomes thermodynamically unstable and the system transitions between two states. This transition is marked by a divergence in the specific heat, which does not have to be accompanied by an order parameter, nor by the full closure of the gap. We illustrate the thermodynamics using a simple two level system and superfluid $^4$He as examples, and we argue that the hidden order transition in URu$_2$Si$_2$ is an example of such an occupancy driven transition in the absence of an order parameter.
item.dc:creator: Ian Madden, Alex Kociubinski, Wouter Montfrooij

item.title: Spin-resolved microscopy of $^{87}$Sr SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard systems
item.description: arXiv:2603.05478v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Quantum-gas microscopes provide direct access to the phases of the Hubbard model, bringing microscopic insight into the complex competition between interactions, SU(2) magnetism, and doping. Alkaline-earth(-like) fermions extend this spin-1/2 paradigm by realizing higher symmetries and giving access to SU($N$) Hubbard models, with rich phase diagrams to be unveiled. Despite its fundamental interest, a microscopic exploration of SU($N$) quantum systems has remained elusive. Here we report the realization of a quantum-gas microscope for fermionic $^{87}$Sr. Our imaging scheme, based on cooling and fluorescence on the narrow intercombination line at 689 nm, enables spin-resolved single-atom detection. By implementing a spin-selective optical pumping protocol, we determine the occupation of each of the 10 spin states in a single experimental realization, a crucial capability for probing site-resolved magnetic correlations. We benchmark our method by observing single-particle Larmor precession across the full spin-9/2 ground-state manifold and use numerical simulations of SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard chains, incorporating the measured detection fidelities, to demonstrate its capability to resolve many-body spin correlations. Our results establish $^{87}$Sr quantum-gas microscopy as a powerful approach to study exotic magnetism in the SU($N$) Fermi-Hubbard model, and provide a new detection tool for studies in quantum simulation, computation, and metrology.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Gas-Ferrer, Antonio Rubio-Abadal, Sandra Buob, Leonardo Bezzo, Jonatan H\"oschele, Leticia Tarruell

item.title: Spinodal-controlled freeze-out and nucleation at the first-order superfluid-supersolid transition of a dipolar gas
item.description: arXiv:2610.12511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Dipolar quantum gases in elongated traps become supersolid through a transition that is continuous at intermediate density but first order at low and high density; at the continuous point, ramps of the scattering length follow Kibble-Zurek scaling. We study ramps across the first-order superfluid-supersolid transition of $^{164}$Dy in an infinite tube using the 3D extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation with truncated-Wigner noise. With quantum noise only, the uniform superfluid survives the metastable window and transforms after its spinodal, where the roton softens. For onsets occurring during the linear ramp, the delay measured from this spinodal has a fitted exponent $\zeta = 0.36 \pm 0.02$, close to the continuous-transition result and the mean-field value $1/3$. Reverse ramps show a comparable delay beyond the fold of the crystal branch, producing dynamical hysteresis. Initial thermal noise with nominal temperatures of 2.5-10 nK produces crystalline regions inside the metastable window during holds, with faster nucleation closer to the spinodal and at higher initial temperature. In ramps at 5 nK, thermal fluctuations make the superfluid fraction $f_s$ cross onset thresholds near $f_s = 1$ early, whereas the bulk of the crystal still forms after the zero-temperature spinodal with a similar scaling. Without a heat bath these effective rates depend on preparation: ramps crossing the window at the same rate nucleate early in 2 of 32 or 11 of 16 realizations depending on their starting point. At low density, slower ramps select larger spacings in a crystal of separated droplets, and droplets survive far above the transition on reverse ramps. A Maxwell construction gives a coexistence window $0.037 a_0$ wide around the first-order transition point, in which localized states exist; in the simulated tube they lie above the homogeneous states. At the continuous point there is no coexistence.
item.dc:creator: Wai Kui Wong

item.title: Near self-duality and spatial reorganization of anyon vortex lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.25412v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Contact attraction drives the self-generated vortex lattice of a trapped anyon gas towards self-duality, but integrated energies do not reveal where the remaining departure from it is located. We address this question in the almost-bosonic Chern--Simons--Schr\"odinger average-field model using a positive, gauge-invariant local defect that measures the covariant kinetic energy in excess of the magnetic bound. Numerically computed low-energy states at three statistical fluxes show that, as the stability line is approached, the integrated defect falls by about two orders of magnitude while the density modulation grows, so that magnetic saturation and density uniformity separate. The residual defect concentrates in a vortex-free outer shell that carries unscreened statistical flux. There it reduces to a smooth radial mismatch between the statistical flow and the density decay, which the interior lattice cannot cancel, whereas the covariant kinetic and amplitude-gradient energies show no comparable enrichment. The effect is robust to grid and box refinement, while its magnitude depends on flux and on the low-energy branch. Exact dilation and contact-response identities relate the squared energy to the density shape and provide consistency checks. Repulsion produces the opposite trend: a smoother density with a larger defect.
item.dc:creator: Bao-Duy Le

item.title: Quantum theory of molecular orientation
item.description: arXiv:2403.04572v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We formulate a quantum phase space for rotational and nuclear-spin states of rigid molecules. For each nuclear spin isomer, we re-derive the isomer's admissible angular momentum states from molecular geometry and nuclear-spin data, introduce its angular position states using quantization theory, and develop a generalized Fourier transform converting between the two. We classify molecules into three types -- asymmetric, rotationally symmetric, and perrotationally symmetric -- with the last type having no macroscopic analogue due to nuclear-spin statistics constraints. We discuss two general features in perrotationally symmetric state spaces that are Hamiltonian-independent and induced solely by symmetry and spin statistics. First, we quantify when and how an isomer's state space is completely rotation-spin entangled, meaning that it does not admit any separable states. Second, we identify isomers whose position states house an internal pseudo-spin or "fiber" degree of freedom, and the fiber's Berry phase or matrix after adiabatic changes in position yields naturally robust operations, akin to braiding anyonic quasiparticles or realizing fault-tolerant quantum gates. We outline how the fiber can be used as a quantum error-correcting code and discuss scenarios where these features can be experimentally probed
item.dc:creator: Victor V. Albert, Eric Kubischta, Mikhail Lemeshko, Lee R. Liu

item.title: Many-body localization
item.description: arXiv:2604.12464v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present an introductory review of nonergodic dynamics in interacting many-body quantum systems, focusing on the phenomenon of many-body localization (MBL). We describe aspects of MBL and summarize the evidence for a crossover from the ergodic to the MBL regime in finite systems, using the paradigmatic XXZ model as an example. We then broaden the scope to other models to illustrate the generality of the phenomenon. We briefly touch on the largely unexplored relation between MBL and quantum computing.
item.dc:creator: Jakub Zakrzewski

item.title: On the Ising/tricritical-Ising interface: From ${W}_3$ symmetry to Rydberg atoms
item.description: arXiv:2605.23848v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We consider interfaces between critical spin-chains in different universality classes, described in the continuum limit by defect/interface conformal field theory (DCFT/ICFT). We focus on a conformal interface between the Tricritical Ising (TIM) and the Ising CFT exploring the possibility of its experimental realizations in the context of Rydberg atom arrays. Our analysis emphasizes non-invertible symmetries and consistency under modular transformations, and uses defect couplings and the defect spectrum -- including in the case of mixed boundary conditions -- to make sharp experimental predictions. The structure of the observables hinges on a newly discovered pattern of emergent ${W}_3$ chiral symmetry for the Tricritical-Ising/Ising interface.
item.dc:creator: Ant\'onio Antunes, Junchen Rong

item.title: Effective field equations with stochastic initial conditions
item.description: arXiv:2608.16486v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The evolution of quantum field expectation values from an initial non-equilibrium quantum state can be followed numerically using the Truncated Wigner technique. It can track non-perturbative quantum phenomena, such as false vacuum decay, in real time with promising results. Nevertheless, it is an approximate method subject to quantum loop corrections. The extension of Truncated Wigner into a fully fledged effective field equation approach is discussed here, including corrections from higher loops and higher momenta.
item.dc:creator: Ian G. Moss
